26-qf1-qb-1455.solution: Breaths = rate × time. Two hours is 2 × 60 = 120 minutes, so breaths = 15 × 120 = 1,800. So the patient takes 1,800 breaths.
26-qf1-qb-1455.trick: 15 × 60 = 900 breaths an hour, so two hours is 1,800. The other options are 6 hours (5,400) and 4 hours (3,600).

26-qf1-qb-1460.solution: The total cost is the integral of the marginal cost from 0 to 6, taking the fixed cost as zero. ∫ from 0 to 6 of (6x + 4) dx = [3x² + 4x] from 0 to 6 = 3(36) + 4(6) = 108 + 24 = 132. So the total cost is 132.
26-qf1-qb-1460.trick: MC is a straight line, so total cost = items × average MC. MC(0) = 4 and MC(6) = 40, so the average is 22, and 6 × 22 = 132.

26-qf1-qb-1464.solution: Relative error = absolute error ÷ actual value. The absolute error is |4.8 − 5.0| = 0.2. So the relative error is 0.2 ÷ 5.0 = 0.04, which is 4%.
26-qf1-qb-1464.trick: 1% of 5 is 0.05, and the error 0.2 is four of those. So 4%.

26-qf1-qb-1475.solution: At 25°C, pH + pOH = 14, so pH = 14 − 10 = 4. The hydrogen ion concentration is 10 raised to the power of −pH, so [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴ M. That is 0.0001 M.
26-qf1-qb-1475.trick: Do 14 − 10 = 4, then write 10⁻⁴, which is 0.0001 (the 1 sits in the fourth decimal place).

26-qf1-qb-1487.solution: Average rate of change = (f(4) − f(1)) ÷ (4 − 1). Here f(1) = 1 − 5 = −4 and f(4) = 16 − 20 = −4. So the rate is (−4 − (−4)) ÷ 3 = 0 ÷ 3 = 0.
26-qf1-qb-1487.trick: x² − 5x has roots 0 and 5, so it is symmetric about 2.5. The ends 1 and 4 are mirror points (1 + 4 = 5), so f(1) = f(4) and the rate is 0.

26-qf1-qb-1504.solution: Convert to centimetres: 2 m = 200 cm. Number of books = 200 ÷ 3.2 = 62.5. Only whole books fit, so round down. The shelf holds 62 books.
26-qf1-qb-1504.trick: Multiply both numbers by 5 to get 1000 ÷ 16. Since 1 ÷ 16 = 0.0625, that is 62.5, so 62 whole books.

26-qf1-qb-1517.solution: The total cost is the integral of the marginal cost from 0 to 5, taking the fixed cost as zero. ∫ from 0 to 5 of (4x + 3) dx = [2x² + 3x] from 0 to 5 = 2(25) + 3(5) = 50 + 15 = 65. So the total cost is 65.
26-qf1-qb-1517.trick: MC is a straight line, so total cost = items × average MC. MC(0) = 3 and MC(5) = 23, so the average is 13, and 5 × 13 = 65.

26-qf1-qb-1527.solution: The ratio 7:3 makes 7 + 3 = 10 parts. The second partner gets 3 parts, which is 3 ÷ 10 × 500,000 = 150,000. So the second partner receives ₦150,000.
26-qf1-qb-1527.trick: One part is ₦500,000 ÷ 10 = ₦50,000. Three parts is ₦150,000.

26-qf1-qb-1535.solution: Test each number after 53. The numbers 54, 56 and 58 are even, 55 ends in 5, and 57 = 3 × 19. The number 59 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 7, so it is prime. So the next prime is 59.
26-qf1-qb-1535.trick: Cross out the evens and 55. The digits of 57 add to 12, so it is a multiple of 3. The next number, 59, is not in the 3, 5 or 7 times tables, so it is prime.

26-qf1-qb-1539.solution: Complete the square: x² − 6x + 10 = (x − 3)² + 1. A square is never negative, so the smallest value is 0 + 1, reached at x = 3. So the minimum value is 1.
26-qf1-qb-1539.trick: Half of 6 is 3, and 3² = 9. The minimum is 10 − 9 = 1.

26-qf1-qb-1546.solution: Put x = 3 into y = √(25 − x²). Then y = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4. So y = 4.
26-qf1-qb-1546.trick: 25 − 9 = 16, and √16 = 4. It is the 3, 4, 5 triangle with hypotenuse 5, so the missing side is 4.

26-qf1-qb-1557.solution: The ball lands when its height is 0. Taking the throw from ground level, the height is s(t) = ∫ v dt = 20t − 4.9t². Setting 20t − 4.9t² = 0 gives t(20 − 4.9t) = 0, so t = 0 or t = 20 ÷ 4.9 ≈ 4.08. So the ball hits the ground after about 4.08 s.
26-qf1-qb-1557.trick: The ball stops rising when v = 0, at t = 20 ÷ 9.8 ≈ 2.04 s. The fall takes as long as the rise, so double it: about 4.08 s. Only one option is above 4 s.

26-qf1-bm-1819.solution: The dot product multiplies matching parts and adds them. A · B = (3)(2) + (4)(−1) = 6 − 4 = 2. So A · B = 2.
26-qf1-bm-1819.trick: Multiply the i parts (3 × 2 = 6) and the j parts (4 × (−1) = −4), then add to get 2. The option 10 is what you get by dropping the minus sign.

26-qf1-bm-1824.solution: Work is the integral of force over distance. W = ∫ from 2 to 4 of 150x dx = [75x²] from 2 to 4 = 75(16) − 75(4) = 1,200 − 300 = 900. So the work done is 900 J.
26-qf1-bm-1824.trick: The force rises in a straight line, so work = average force × distance. The average force is F(3) = 450, and the distance is 2 m, so 450 × 2 = 900 J.

26-qf1-bm-1829.solution: Acid:water = 5:3, so water = acid × 3 ÷ 5. That is 25 × 3 ÷ 5 = 75 ÷ 5 = 15. So 15 L of water is needed.
26-qf1-bm-1829.trick: 25 L is 5 parts, so one part is 5 L. Water is 3 parts, which is 3 × 5 = 15 L.

26-qf1-bm-1834.solution: Take 800 MW as the electrical output. At 30% efficiency the input is 800 ÷ 0.3 ≈ 2,667 MW, so the waste heat is 2,667 − 800 ≈ 1,867 MW. Over one hour, energy = power × time = 1,867 MW × 1 h. So the waste heat is about 1,867 MWh.
26-qf1-bm-1834.trick: Waste ÷ output = 70 ÷ 30 = 7/3. So waste = 800 × 7/3 = 1,600 + 267 ≈ 1,867. The options 1,801 and 1,808 are too small.

26-qf1-bm-1841.trick: Write −x² + 200x as x(200 − x), which is 40 × 160 = 6,400. Then subtract 100 to get 6,300.

26-qf1-bm-1849.solution: Marginal profit is the derivative of P(x). P′(x) = −2x + 50, so P′(20) = −40 + 50 = 10. So the marginal profit at x = 20 is 10.
26-qf1-bm-1849.trick: Differentiate in your head: −x² becomes −2x, 50x becomes 50 and −100 disappears. So 50 − 2 × 20 = 10.

26-qf1-bm-1857.solution: Pick 4 of the 8 engineers and the other 2 places from the 10 analysts. The number of teams is C(8,4) × C(10,2) = 70 × 45 = 3,150. So 3,150 teams have exactly 4 engineers.

26-qf1-bm-1864.solution: Expand: (2 + 3i)(1 − i) = 2 − 2i + 3i − 3i². Since i² = −1, the last term −3i² becomes +3. So the product is 2 + 3 + i = 5 + i.
26-qf1-bm-1864.trick: Real part: 2 + 3 = 5, because −3i² = +3. Imaginary part: 3i − 2i = i. Only the option 5 + i has real part 5.

26-qf1-bm-1871.solution: A line with slope m and y intercept c is y = mx + c. The point (0, 4) lies on the y axis, so c = 4. With m = −2, the line is y = −2x + 4.
26-qf1-bm-1871.trick: (0, 4) is the y intercept, so the number added at the end is 4. The other options give 2 and 6 at x = 0.

26-qf1-bm-1879.trick: For ax² + bx + c between p and q, the average rate is a(p + q) + b. That is 3 × (1 + 4) − 1 = 14.

26-qf1-bm-1886.solution: Use the chain rule. The outer function sin becomes cos, keeping the inside x² + 3x. Then multiply by the derivative of the inside, which is 2x + 3. So f′(x) = (2x + 3)cos(x² + 3x).
26-qf1-bm-1886.trick: Keep the inside, change sin to cos, then multiply by the derivative of the inside. The option 2x cos 3x changes the inside, and cos(x² + 3x) has no (2x + 3) factor.

26-qf1-bm-1895.solution: Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, aA and aa, a genotype ratio of 1:2:1. With A completely dominant, AA and Aa look the same, so 3 show the dominant trait and 1 shows the recessive trait. So the phenotypic ratio is 3:1.
26-qf1-bm-1895.trick: Only one gene is involved, so 9:3:3:1 (two genes) is out. 1:2:1 counts genotypes, but phenotype means what you see, so the answer is 3:1.

26-qf1-bm-1901.solution: The magnitude of a cross product is |A × B| = |A||B| sin θ. For perpendicular vectors θ = 90° and sin 90° = 1. So |A × B| = 5 × 5 × 1 = 25.
26-qf1-bm-1901.trick: Perpendicular means sin 90° = 1, so just multiply the lengths: 5 × 5 = 25.

26-qf1-bm-1906.solution: Each year the value falls by 10% of its current value, so it is multiplied by 0.9 each year. After 2 years the value is 1,000,000 × 0.9² = 1,000,000 × 0.81 = 810,000. So the car is worth ₦810,000.
26-qf1-bm-1906.trick: Take 10% off twice. ₦1,000,000 becomes ₦900,000, then 10% of ₦900,000 is ₦90,000, which leaves ₦810,000.

26-qf3-qb-1554.solution: A perpetuity pays the same amount every year forever, so PV = payment ÷ rate, with the first payment a year from now. PV = 5,000 ÷ 0.08 = 62,500. So the present value is ₦62,500.
26-qf3-qb-1554.trick: Dividing by 0.08 is dividing by 8 and then multiplying by 100. 5,000 ÷ 8 = 625, so the answer is 62,500.

26-qf3-qb-1607.solution: Simple interest I = P × R × T, so R = I ÷ (P × T). The interest is 9,600 − 8,000 = 1,600. So R = 1,600 ÷ (8,000 × 4) = 1,600 ÷ 32,000 = 0.05, which is 5% a year.
26-qf3-qb-1607.trick: The interest 1,600 is 20% of 8,000. That took 4 years, so 20 ÷ 4 = 5% a year.

26-qf3-qb-2004.solution: Simple interest I = P × R × T, so T = I ÷ (P × R). T = 3,000 ÷ (15,000 × 0.05) = 3,000 ÷ 750 = 4. So it takes 4 years.

26-qf3-bm-2584.solution: Each year the value falls by 10% of its current value, so it is multiplied by 0.9 each year. After 2 years the value is 3,000,000 × 0.9² = 3,000,000 × 0.81 = 2,430,000. So the car is worth ₦2,430,000.
26-qf3-bm-2584.trick: 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, and 3 × 0.81 = 2.43, so ₦2,430,000. The option ₦2,400,000 takes a flat 20% off the original price, which ignores that the second 10% is of a smaller value.
